title: The program BRD has no requirement section for P9 reporting
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5
description: Section 5 of the program BRD carries 16 requirement sections and no P9 section; section 11 states that P9, P8 and P10 have no row of their own and that the steering and management information duties are carried inside 5.3, 5.6 and 5.7. There is therefore no REQ- prefix that belongs to reporting, and the requirement keys this PRD traces to are the epic-level keys (RWB-E1-013, RWB-E2-009, BR-061, BR-082, BR-083) plus three supporting program keys.
evidence: Program v5 section 5 (5.1 to 5.16), section 10.2 row RWB-SVC-P9, section 11 note; the BRD's own row CG-B-REQ-BRD-PROG-8 records the same fact
proposed: Keep the epic-level keys as the trace target and state the coverage basis in section 11.2 until a P9 requirement section exists

title: FSD P9 has no requirement IDs, so FR rows cannot map to FSD REQ IDs
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P9 Reporting v3
description: The 'Requirements served' table of FSD P9 is present and empty. The FSD carries feature IDs (FEAT-RPT-01 to FEAT-RPT-10) and acceptance criteria IDs (AC-P9-xxx) but no REQ- IDs. The work package asks for FR rows mapped to FSD REQ IDs; there are none to map to, so every FR row names the FSD feature and acceptance criterion it comes from instead.
evidence: FSD P9 'Requirements served' table with a header and no rows; A1.2 feature overview; A2.1 to A2.10
proposed: Trace FR rows to FEAT-RPT-nn and AC-P9-nnn-nn; add REQ IDs to the FSD if a program-level key is needed

title: The data lake and the Power BI connection are removed but the whole reporting FSD is built on them
source: Architecture v5; FSD P9 Reporting v3
section: Arch v5 slides 15, 37 and 41; FSD A2.1 to A2.8
description: ADR-018 and DP-17 remove the data lake and the Power BI feed (INT-19, INT-20). FSD P9 names 'Power BI, Data lake' as the integration points of A2.1, A2.3, A2.4, A2.5, A2.7 and A2.8, AC-ALT-P9-001-02 tests an INT-19 extract in the data lake, AC-EXC-P9-001-03 tests a data lake that does not answer, and AC-P9-004-01 and AC-ALT-P9-004-01 test lake partitions and the archive tier. Architecture v5 gives rwb-reporting the dashboard and report resources and a delivered file instead.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 37 'Data lake and Power BI feed (INT-19/20) to Removed: reports from rwb-reporting'; slide 15 P9 OUT (deliverFile); FSD P9 A2.1.2, A2.3.2, A2.4.2, A2.5.2, A2.7.2, A2.8.2
proposed: Read every Power BI and data lake destination as the reporting read model served on the gateway-bff route, and every lake delivery as a file delivered by rwb-integration

title: JOB-15 is described both as a Temporal Schedule at 01:30 and as an Airflow trigger
source: Architecture v5; Batch and Scheduling Design v4
description: Slide 15 gives rwb-reporting 'Temporal Schedule: measures 01:30' together with 'Act: buildRegulatoryExtract'. Slide 44 gives JOB-15 as 'Airflow trigger (no data lake)' at 01:30, and slide 31 note 3 sends the report and regulatory extract through POST /v1/reports/{id}/run. Batch and Scheduling Design v4 writes the extract to the data lake nightly. Three mechanisms are named for one job.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 15 IN line; slide 31 note 3; slide 44 JOB-15; Ownership Map ruling on JOB-15
owner_role: Solution architect with the bank platform team
proposed: Build the schedule at 01:30 and the run operation as the same run's two entries, and let the owner pick the live path

title: The report resource path differs between the architecture and the ownership map
source: Architecture v5; Ownership Map v1; API Specification v4
description: Arch v5 gives P9 the resources GET /dashboards/{id}, GET /reports/{id} and POST /reports/{id}/run. The Ownership Map and API Specification v4 carry GET /reports/measures. It is not stated what value {id} takes, or whether the measure read is a separate resource from the report read.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 15 IN line and slide 41 catalogue row P9 (/dashboards/{id}); Ownership Map api entry 'GET /reports/measures'
proposed: Keep both paths in the contract, read /reports/{id} as /reports/measures for the measure report, and confirm the identifier

title: The measure set is six definitions in one acceptance criterion and seven measures in another
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P9 Reporting v3
description: AC-P9-001-01 defines six measures (CASES_BY_ROUTE, CASES_BY_AGE, CASES_BY_QUEUE, REALIZED_RECOVERY, TIME_IN_STAGE, TAT_BY_ROUTE). AC-P9-003-01 and AC-P9-008-01 expect a value 'for each of the 7 measures'. AC-ALT-P9-003-01 adds CASES_BY_STAGE and DECISIONS_LOGGED, and AC-ALT-P9-003-02 adds AGENT_ACCEPTANCE and AGENT_OVERRIDE. The seventh measure is never named.
owner_role: Tribe lead with the Reporting and BI analyst
proposed: Publish the six baseline measures plus CASES_BY_STAGE, DECISIONS_LOGGED and the two agent measures, and carry the count as an open question

title: RWB-E1-014 is retired but the operations reporting of P9 is built on the copy it produced
source: Business Requirements Epic 1 v5; FSD P9 Reporting v3; Architecture v5
description: D-RCV-60 retires RWB-E1-014 (decision log copy to the data lake) and REQ-DRI-009 shares its subject; ADR-018 removes the data lake and decision-log ingest becomes continuous from Kafka in rwb-decision. FEAT-RPT-04 (operations reporting from the decision log) is still specified on that copy, and AC-P9-004-01, AC-ALT-P9-004-01, AC-ALT-P9-004-02 and AC-EXC-P9-004-01 to -06 test the partition, the manifest, the watermark and REC-08.
evidence: Epic 1 v5 section 8.5 row RWB-E1-014 (no story: retired); FSD P9 A2.4 and its acceptance criteria; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-13 'ingest is continuous (Kafka)'
proposed: Build the operational measures from the decision record received on rwb.decision-record.v1, and carry the copy's checks as the extract's own reconciliation

title: The reconciliation and the data quality break are P1's, but FSD P9 specifies them as its own features
source: Ownership Map v1; FSD P9 Reporting v3; Business Requirements Epic 1 v5
section: Ownership Map tables and jobs; FSD A2.5 and A2.9
description: reconciliation_result and JOB-04 belong to P1 rwb-source-data, and RWB-E1-011 is traced to RWB-SVC-P1. FSD P9 carries FEAT-RPT-05 (reconcile case counts across sources) and FEAT-RPT-09 (manage a data quality break), with acceptance criteria on the reconciliation, the break rows and the hold. It is not stated which service owns the break record that a steward works to closure.
evidence: Ownership Map tables (reconciliation_result, owner P1); Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-04 owner rwb-source-data; Epic 1 v5 section 9 row RWB-E1-011 to RWB-SVC-P1; FSD P9 A2.5 and A2.9
owner_role: Data steward and data product owner
proposed: Read the reconciliation result and the break rows from P1's contract and hold the break view and the closure in P9

title: Queue depth and ageing are computed in P3 and published in P9
source: Ownership Map v1; FSD P9 Reporting v3
description: queue_measure belongs to P3 rwb-case, which publishes queue measures to the case list and to reporting (FEAT-CWC-18, JOB-06). FSD P9 FEAT-RPT-02 publishes queue depth, ageing and the owner spread for every team, and its acceptance criteria include a rebalancing run and capacity caps. One measure with two owners.
evidence: Ownership Map tables (queue_measure, owner P3); FSD P9 A2.2 and AC-P9-002-01, AC-ALT-P9-002-01, AC-ALT-P9-002-02
proposed: P3 computes and this service publishes the queue measures on the business date, reading the case list count for the reconciliation

title: Classification, staging and re-ageing sit in P9's FSD but not in the architecture's P9 scope
source: Architecture v5; FSD P9 Reporting v3; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1
section: Arch v5 slide 41; FSD A2.10; BR-083
description: Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-reporting measures, snapshots, the steering dashboard and regulatory reports. FSD P9 A2.10 (FEAT-RPT-10) applies the classification, staging and re-ageing rules and recomputes the segment, and BR-083 with RWB-E8-002 depends on it. The split plan gives P9 the primary. No service is named for classification and re-ageing in the architecture.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 row P9; FSD P9 A2.10; Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 8.6 BR-083 and section 14.1
proposed: Build it in P9 under BR-083 pending confirmation, and confirm whether the duty should sit with the case or the source-data service

title: No field catalog exists for the snapshot, the publication, the report definition, the run record or the projections
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P9 Reporting v3
description: The FSD gives one field catalog of eight fields, and it is the measure_definition catalog repeated in three sections. measure_snapshot, measure_publish, the report and return definitions, the extract run record and the read-model projections have no field list beyond the attributes named in the acceptance criteria.
evidence: FSD P9 A2.3.3.2, A2.6.3.2, A2.9.3.2 (the same eight measure_definition fields); the acceptance criteria name business_date, definition_version, freshness stamp and row count only
proposed: Carry the named attributes in this PRD and take the rest from the technical specification and the logical data model

title: No retention class or retention period is set for a snapshot, an extract or a run record
source: Business Requirements Program v5; FSD P9 Reporting v3
section: Program v5 6.5 (NFR-028 to NFR-031, NFR-075); DL26
description: DL26 asks how long each data product and document type is kept and which fields are masked for which role, and it is unanswered. NFR-030 and NFR-031 carry open periods. The reporting entities therefore carry a class and an open period, and a disposal cannot yet be proved.
evidence: Program v5 6.5 NFR-030, NFR-031 status Open DL26; section 9 DL26
proposed: Declare a class per entity now, and apply the periods from DL26 when they are set

title: No benefit model measures, baselines or targets are set for benefit realisation
source: Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1
description: BR-061 requires benefit realisation monthly against the baseline and KPI-014 records 'Tracked monthly, targets not set'. Q-020 asks which benefit model measures and baselines apply and is unanswered. A benefit view cannot state a variance without them.
evidence: Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-061, KPI-014, Q-020 (CG-B-REQ-BRD-E38-20)
proposed: Report each measured value against the frozen baseline and state where no target exists

title: The regulatory extract has no agreed source after the data lake is removed
source: Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1; FSD P9 Reporting v3
description: BR-082 requires the returns to be produced from the data products and the decision log, and FEAT-RPT-07 names a data lake that ADR-018 removes. Q-018 asks where the regulatory extracts read from and is unanswered, so the source of the return items is open.
evidence: Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-018 (CG-B-REQ-BRD-E38-18) and BR-082; FSD P9 A2.7 integration points
proposed: Build the return from the reporting read model and the decision record and deliver it as a file

title: SCR-37 has no owner and no serving path
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P9 Reporting v3; Architecture v5
section: FSD Screens; Arch v5 slide 41 and DP-19
description: FSD P9 lists one screen, SCR-37 Steering dashboard, with no statement of who serves it. Architecture v5 gives rwb-reporting the dashboard resource and the edge the composite route, and gives rwb-case the queue and case views. Whether the dashboard is a page served by this service or a composition at the edge is not stated.
evidence: FSD P9 Screens table; Arch v5 slide 41 row P9 (/dashboards/{id}); DP-19; Arch v5 slide 13 reading tip
proposed: Serve the dashboard data set and the report reads on this service's resources behind the gateway-bff route

title: No target is set for agent acceptance and override
source: Business Requirements Program v5; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1
section: Program v5 6.12 NFR-066; Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-026
description: NFR-066 requires acceptance, override rate, latency and cost to be measured and reported per agent and asks for no target. Q-026 asks what targets apply and is unanswered. The FSD states only that an agent with no runs shows 'No runs'.
evidence: Program v5 NFR-066; Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-026 (CG-B-REQ-BRD-E38-26); FSD P9 AC-EXC-P9-003-02
proposed: Publish the two rates per agent and version and set no threshold until one is agreed

title: Message IDs from other modules are reused by P9's validation rules
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P9 Reporting v3
description: The validation rules of P9 use MSG-P1-001 for a stale data product, MSG-P1-012 for the reconciliation hold, MSG-P1-019 for a failed row-count check, MSG-P3-029 for a queue depth difference, MSG-P3-028 and MSG-P3-011 for queue breaches and capacity, MSG-P2-006 for a concurrent run and MSG-P7-003 for a missing decision record. Only MSG-P9-002 and MSG-P9-003 belong to this module.
proposed: Keep every message ID as written in the FSD and treat it as a shared message, not a copy

title: No approval is recorded for this PRD
source: D-RCV-60 overlay; Template and Rules v1 section R8.1
description: The playbook gate requires a Product Owner and FDA decision before the requirements are approved. This run proceeds without human approval by the D-RCV-60 overlay, so the approval table is empty and the document stays Draft.
evidence: Run overlay D-RCV-60 (no human approval in this run); Template and Rules v1 R8.1
proposed: Record the Product Owner and FDA decision before wave 1 build starts

title: RWB-E2-009 promises a Power BI data set, which ADR-018 removes
source: Business Requirements Epic 2 v3; Architecture v5
section: Epic 2 v3 section 3.9; Arch v5 slide 37
description: RWB-E2-009 asks for 'a Power BI data set for the steering dashboard'. Architecture v5 removes the Power BI feed (INT-19/20) and gives rwb-reporting the dashboard and report resources with the edge in front. The requirement's outcome survives; its stated delivery vehicle does not.
evidence: Epic 2 v3 section 3.9 row RWB-E2-009; Arch v5 slide 37; FSD P9 AC-P9-003-01 (07:30 Power BI refresh)
proposed: Read the data set as this service's dashboard and measure resources, read through gateway-bff

title: No event source is named for the agent acceptance and override measures
source: Architecture v5
description: EV-28 AgentRunCompleted lists rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation as consumers, and the consumer matrix gives rwb-reporting no dependency on rwb-agent. FSD P9 nevertheless publishes AGENT_ACCEPTANCE and AGENT_OVERRIDE per agent version, and RWB-E2-009 asks for agent acceptance in the data set.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 row 28 consumers; slide 13 consumer matrix row P9 (no P10 column set); FSD P9 AC-ALT-P9-003-02
owner_role: Solution architect with the AI product owner
proposed: Count the two rates from the decision record, which carries the agent and prompt version, the recommendation, the approval and the outcome
